claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a nanocrystalline structure.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has random grain boundaries.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has minimal surface oxide.
Post-deposition annealing promotes grain-boundary stabilization in FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Post-deposition annealing promotes selective oxidation primarily of Cu.
Annealing enables formation of a continuous, thin Cu oxide scale during high-temperature sliding.
Increasing annealing time or temperature promotes grain growth refinement.
The Cu oxide layer acts as a lubricious protective barrier.
The Cu oxide layer suppresses direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
Annealing and oxide formation shift deformation from dislocation glide to grain-boundary-mediated sliding.
The annealed coating develops an intergranular-fracture deformation signature.
The combined oxide barrier and deformation transition reduce material removal and lower wear rate.
The annealed coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
The coefficient of friction may increase because of tribochemical surface reactions.
The as-deposited baseline is predominantly deformed by dislocation motion.
The as-deposited baseline has higher wear than the annealed coating.
The predictions apply to thin coatings sliding at 300–600 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
The predictions may not apply in inert atmospheres or at substantially lower temperatures because oxidation is suppressed.

contradictions.description: The intervention says annealing promotes 'grain growth refinement,' conflating grain growth with refinement, while the baseline is described as having finer grains and the annealed mediator remains nanocrystalline. The intended direction of grain-size change is therefore internally unclear.
